subject: Biology
topic: Vitamins and deficiency diseases — mixed tiers
description: Fat-soluble vs water-soluble, Vitamin A/B/C/D/E/K and their deficiency diseases, sources

questions.stem: Vitamin C deficiency causes which classical disease?

options.option_text: Beri-beri, with weakness in legs and arms
Scurvy, with bleeding gums and skin spots
Rickets, with bowed legs and softened bones
Pellagra, with skin rash and chronic diarrhoea

questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) — needed for collagen synthesis. Deficiency → SCURVY: bleeding gums, loose teeth, slow wound healing, skin haemorrhages. Sources: citrus fruits, amla, guava, capsicum, broccoli. Lind's 1747 trial on British sailors using lemons → first controlled trial. Distractor 1 = vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency. Distractor 3 = vitamin D / calcium deficiency in children. Distractor 4 = vitamin B3 (niacin) deficiency.

options.option_text: Goitre, an enlarged thyroid gland in the neck
Night-blindness and dry eyes (xerophthalmia)
Megaloblastic anaemia with very large red cells
Haemorrhagic disease with prolonged bleeding times

questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) — needed for rhodopsin synthesis in retinal rods → low-light vision. Deficiency → NIGHT BLINDNESS, then xerophthalmia (dry eyes), Bitot's spots, eventually keratomalacia + blindness. Sources: liver, milk, eggs; carotenoids in carrots, papaya, mango, dark-green leafy vegetables (body converts beta-carotene to vitamin A). Distractor 1 = iodine deficiency (goitre). Distractor 3 = vitamin B12 / folate deficiency. Distractor 4 = vitamin K deficiency.

questions.stem: Vitamin D is unique among vitamins because the body can:

options.option_text: Store unlimited amounts of it without any toxicity
Synthesise it in the skin when exposed to sunlight UV-B
Excrete excess of it freely through sweat as needed
Convert it instantly into protein for immediate use

questions.explanation: Vitamin D — endogenous synthesis: 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin → previtamin D₃ via UV-B (290-315 nm) → cholecalciferol → activated to calcitriol in liver + kidney. Required for calcium absorption from gut. Deficiency → RICKETS in children (soft bowed legs), OSTEOMALACIA in adults. Indians often deficient despite plenty of sunshine (skin pigmentation, indoor lifestyles, modesty clothing). Sources besides sunlight: fortified milk, egg yolk, fatty fish, mushrooms. Distractor 1 — fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) DO accumulate and CAN be toxic in excess. Distractor 3 — vitamins aren't excreted via sweat. Distractor 4 — vitamins are not protein.

questions.stem: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is special because it is:

options.option_text: The only vitamin synthesised by green plants in chloroplasts
Found mainly in animal foods, problematic for strict vegans
Manufactured by the human liver from raw amino acids
Destroyed completely by even gentle cooking heat

questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 — only vitamin produced by BACTERIA / ARCHAEA, not by plants or animals directly. Found in: meat, fish, eggs, dairy. STRICT VEGANS need B12 supplements or fortified foods. Deficiency → megaloblastic / pernicious anaemia, neuropathy, dementia. Absorption needs INTRINSIC FACTOR (a glycoprotein from stomach parietal cells); autoimmune attack on these cells → pernicious anaemia. Distractor 1 — plants don't make B12. Distractor 3 — liver can store B12 (3-5 yrs supply) but doesn't synthesise it. Distractor 4 — relatively heat-stable, surviving normal cooking.

questions.stem: BERI-BERI is caused by deficiency of which vitamin?

options.option_text: Vitamin C, also called ascorbic acid
Vitamin B1, also called thiamine
Vitamin D, the sunshine vitamin
Vitamin K, needed for clotting

questions.explanation: Beri-beri = thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Two forms: WET BERI-BERI (heart failure, oedema) and DRY BERI-BERI (peripheral neuropathy — weakness in legs, sensory loss, paralysis). Common where polished white rice replaces whole grains (the bran with thiamine is removed). Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (alcoholic neuropathy) is also a thiamine deficiency. Sources: whole grains, legumes, nuts, pork. Distractor 1 = scurvy. Distractor 3 = rickets/osteomalacia. Distractor 4 = bleeding tendency.

options.option_text: Vision in dim light, by acting on retinal rods
Blood clotting, via synthesis of clotting factors
Calcium absorption from food in the small intestine
Energy release from carbohydrates in the cells

questions.explanation: Vitamin K (Koagulation, German) — needed for hepatic synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X (and proteins C and S). Newborns are routinely given a Vitamin K injection at birth to prevent haemorrhagic disease. WARFARIN (anti-coagulant) works as a vitamin K antagonist. Sources: green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale), eggs, liver; gut bacteria also make some. Distractor 1 = vitamin A. Distractor 3 = vitamin D. Distractor 4 = vitamin B-complex (esp. B1 thiamine).

questions.stem: Among the following, which vitamin is FAT-soluble (NOT water-soluble)?

options.option_text: Vitamin C, the antioxidant in citrus fruits
Vitamin E, an antioxidant for cell membranes
Vitamin B-complex, used for energy metabolism
Vitamin B9 (folic acid), needed in pregnancy

questions.explanation: FAT-SOLUBLE vitamins: A, D, E, K (mnemonic 'ADEK'). Stored in body fat + liver; can accumulate to toxic levels if over-supplemented. Need dietary fat for absorption. WATER-SOLUBLE: vitamin C and the B-complex (B1 thiamine, B2 riboflavin, B3 niacin, B5 pantothenic acid, B6 pyridoxine, B7 biotin, B9 folate, B12 cobalamin). Excess water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine; toxicity is rare. Vitamin E (tocopherol) protects cell membranes from oxidative damage.
